compositions.title: Food and water for the journey
compositions.text: Se mann cwæð: ‘Ic wille faran. Mīn scip is gearu. Cumað and helpað mē.’ Twēgen gefēran cōmon tō helpanne. Se mann cwæð: ‘Nimað ðone męte and berað hine. Giefað ðǣm fuglum ðæt wæter.’ Se gefēra cwæð: ‘Ic mæg ðone męte beran. Wē sculon ðæt weorc gefręmman.’ Ðā gefēran bǣron ðone męte and gēafon ðǣm fuglum ðæt wæter. Se mann cwæð: ‘Sittað and etað.’ Ðā gefēran ǣton. Hīe fōron.
compositions.intended_meaning: The man said: ‘I want to travel. My ship is ready. Come and help me.’ Two companions came to help. The man said: ‘Take the food and carry it. Give the birds the water.’ The companion said: ‘I can carry the food. We must perform the work.’ The companions carried the food and gave the birds the water. The man said: ‘Sit and eat.’ The companions ate. They travelled.
audit_requests: Verify complete imperative pairs for cuman, helpan, niman, beran, giefan, sittan and etan; the passage uses the plural cells.
Verify tō helpanne as purposive inflected infinitive with the same human subject as cōmon; no indirect-question or content clause.
Verify willan+faran for volition, magan+beran for physical ability and sculan+gefręmman for obligation.
Extend taught cweðan direct quotation explicitly to taught commands; prior indicative quotation alone does not cover these.
All ordinary lexical arguments and nouns are earlier taught: accusative food/water, dative help-recipient and gift-recipient; grammatical reference hine to masculine męte.
The final plural hīe can include the participants contextually; a question should not demand a uniquely encoded antecedent.
Assess naturalness: the birds receive the water, the companions receive the food, and the journey follows their meal. No new directional phrase or purpose of the ship is asserted.

teaching_examples.text: Ic cann swimman. Hē mæg ðæt wæter beran.
teaching_examples.meaning: I know how to swim. He can carry the water.

new_targets: willan preterite volition + plain infinitive; no automatic future-in-the-past claim

teaching_examples.text: Nim ðone męte. Nimað ðone męte.
teaching_examples.meaning: Take the food, one addressee. Take the food, several addressees.
new_targets: niman complete imperative pair and number of addressees

teaching_examples.text: Gief mē ðæt wæter. Helpað mē.
teaching_examples.meaning: Give me the water, one addressee. Help me, several addressees.
new_targets: helpan plural imperative; prior dative recipients

teaching_examples.meaning: Do not drink the water, one addressee.
new_targets: negative imperative, only if independently evidenced
elementary purpose with tō + inflected infinitive

teaching_examples.meaning: Go. Do the work well, one addressee.
new_targets: gān/dōn imperative; dōn ordinary accusative object

teaching_examples.meaning: The ship will be ready, in an explicitly expected later situation.
new_targets: Elementary future-state indicative bēon with prior predicate-adjective agreement; this is not a universal eom=now/bēon=future rule.
